newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran oil workers back at work, others stay in jail.
newsitem.headline: Iran oil workers back at work, others stay in jail.

text.p: Most oil workers who held a protest at Iran's oil ministry on Sunday have returned to work, but a number who had been arrested remained behind bars, an employee at the National Iranian Oil Company said on Monday.
The NIOC employee gave no figures. Witnesses had said police in riot gear arrested four or five busloads of oil workers demonstrating to press for higher wages.
Witnesses said more than 1,000 workers from Tehran refinery, Iran's third largest, had taken part in the protest.
It was not immediately clear whether the strike had affected work at the refinery, which has a capacity of 225,000 barrels per day (bpd).
It was also not clear whether NIOC and the workers had reached any agreement.

The Tehran refinery workers were protesting against the failure of officials to deliver on promises made last month to meet some of their demands for pay rises, food coupons and housing loans, an oil ministry employee told Reuters.
The workers were also protesting against pressure put on their leaders to resign from their posts at the refinery's union, said the employee, who was not involved in the protests.

NIOC officials in January denied reports of a workers' strike at the 40,000 bpd Shiraz refinery after France' General Labour Confederation called on Iran to respond favourably to demands made by the employees at Shiraz as well as at refineries in Tehran, Tabriz and Isfahan.
Iran -- the world's third biggest oil exporter -- regularly exports fuel oil and middle distillates from its eight refineries which have a capacity of 1.2 million bpd.
